top-10-osint-tools.title: Choose an OSINT tool for the question
top-10-osint-tools.description: A four-step guide to choosing public-source research tools, checking sources and keeping uncertain results separate.
steps: Define the question
Decide whether you need username leads, web history, media verification or source relationships.
Choose the tool
Match the tool to that question. MyRecon is third in our disclosed publisher-selected list.
Open the source
Inspect the original page. A returned link is a lead, not proof of account ownership.
Record the limits
Keep blocks, missing context and uncertain connections in the evidence record.

best-username-search-tools.title: Evaluate a username search tool
best-username-search-tools.description: A known-account exercise for comparing username checkers without confusing profile presence with identity or name availability.
steps: Use a known account
Start with a handle and account you control so you have a reference for the result.
Inspect source links
Open reported profiles and check the exact destination instead of trusting a result count.
Read unknowns
A block, login wall or timeout is inconclusive. It does not prove an account is absent.
Compare the fit
Review setup, exports, coverage and access limits before choosing your workflow.

social-media-osint-tools.title: Build a social media research workflow
social-media-osint-tools.description: Separate public-profile discovery, mentions and media verification while retaining the original source and access context.
steps: Set the scope
Define the public claim or account you are authorized to review before choosing a tool.
Separate the tasks
Use profile discovery for handles, indexed search for mentions and media tools for images.
Keep the context
Record the exact URL, date and whether the view is public or requires account access.
Verify the claim
A matching handle or photo is a clue. Check independent evidence before connecting accounts.

free-osint-tools-for-beginners.title: Start a small OSINT practice exercise
free-osint-tools-for-beginners.description: Use your own known account to practice public-source discovery, verification and evidence logging with free tools.
steps: Start with your account
Use an account you own and a small research question with a known answer.
Try one method
Choose browser search or a documented local tool. Check access limits before running it.
Check the original
Open the source and compare the result with your own account records.
Write what you learned
Record supported observations, unknown checks and what the tool could not establish.

sherlock-vs-maigret-vs-myrecon.title: Compare three username research workflows
sherlock-vs-maigret-vs-myrecon.description: Compare documented setup and reporting choices while using the same known handles and preserving ambiguous outcomes.
steps: Choose a common scope
Select known handles and supported sites. Keep the comparison question consistent.
Record setup and access
Note versions, timeouts and conditions. Local tools and browser previews have different limits.
Review every lead
Verify exact profile URLs and separate unknown responses from supported matches.
Avoid a broad ranking
A small exercise or one case study cannot establish accuracy across every platform.

osint-tools-for-journalists.title: Verify a public claim before publishing
osint-tools-for-journalists.description: A claim-led newsroom workflow that separates discovery, original-source checks, media context and supported conclusions.
steps: Write the claim
Define exactly what needs verification and the public evidence that could support it.
Find the source
Use indexed search, archives or profile leads to locate original material.
Check date and context
Compare the source, capture date and media context. Reused content can describe another event.
Separate fact and inference
Keep source URLs and limitations. Publish only the conclusion your evidence supports.

instagram-username-search.title: Check an Instagram username
instagram-username-search.description: Use an exact handle and the official Instagram destination while keeping unavailable profiles and account ownership unresolved.
steps: Copy the exact handle
Keep dots, underscores and digits. A display name is different from a username.
Use the official profile
Open Instagram search or the profile destination and confirm the domain.
Describe your access
Record a visible page, a login wall or an unavailable destination without guessing the cause.
Confirm the association
Use an owner-published link or your own account records. A handle alone does not prove identity.

instagram-osint-public-profile-guide.title: Keep an Instagram public-profile evidence record
instagram-osint-public-profile-guide.description: Record visible public observations with access context and distinguish source evidence from uncertain associations.
steps: Define the public question
Keep the review limited to information you are authorized to inspect.
Record the visible view
Note the profile URL, observation date and whether you are signed out or an approved follower.
Separate evidence and inference
A visible link supports a public association. Similar names and photos can be copied.
Keep restrictions intact
Private posts and messages remain outside public-source research. Preserve unresolved checks.

reverse-username-search.title: Review a reverse username lookup
reverse-username-search.description: Treat a known username as a discovery starting point rather than a guarantee of identity, phone numbers or email addresses.
steps: Start with a known handle
Record where the handle came from and the purpose of your authorized review.
Find candidate pages
Search supported public destinations and keep the exact URLs returned.
Check independent links
Review owner-declared links and source context before associating accounts.
Keep the conclusion narrow
Username reuse does not identify a person or guarantee their email address or phone number.

social-media-username-search.title: Review a handle across social platforms
social-media-username-search.description: Check exact handles across public sources, review ambiguous responses and distinguish profile presence from registration availability.
steps: List your known handles
Use exact handles you control or have permission to research, not guessed personal details.
Search public destinations
Use supported profile checks and retain the source address for each lead.
Review each response
Open source pages. Login walls, blocks and timeouts remain inconclusive.
Separate the questions
Profile presence, ownership and whether a name can be registered require different evidence.

digital-footprint-checker.title: Turn a footprint check into a cleanup plan
digital-footprint-checker.description: Review your own public accounts, prioritize exposure you control and recheck the original sources after cleanup.
steps: Start with your records
List your own handles, public profiles and accounts you can verify through saved records.
Review public exposure
Inspect source pages and note personal details that reach a wider audience than intended.
Choose a cleanup action
Secure, edit or close confirmed accounts through official controls you can access.
Recheck the source
Confirm the visible change. Missing checker results do not prove that all copies disappeared.

instagram-stalking-and-privacy.title: Respond to unwanted Instagram contact
instagram-stalking-and-privacy.description: Focus on observed behaviour, safe evidence retention, official controls and exposure you can reduce without identifying a visitor.
steps: Describe the behaviour
Record specific unwanted contact. A username does not identify a visitor or establish intent.
Keep evidence when safe
Retain relevant URLs, dates and context privately. Do not expand the review into unrelated people.
Use official controls
Review blocking, reporting, tags and message controls in Instagram's current settings.
Reduce your exposure
Review your own public details and account security. No tool can guarantee a list of profile visitors.
